title: Al-Aqsa Mosque
summary: The Aqsa (Qibli) Mosque is the main prayer hall on the southern side of the Haram al-Sharif in Jerusalem's Old City. Sources attribute the building to the Umayyad caliphs Abd al-Malik and his son al-Walid I. Earthquakes, the Crusader period and later dynasties' repairs reshaped it, and a seven-aisle plan survives from the Fatimid rebuilding.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree on whether Abd al-Malik (685-705), al-Walid I (705-715), or both built it; Archnet dates a major phase to 709-715. Span covers both reigns. Earlier tradition credits Umar (634-644) with a first prayer hall.

when.display: Built under Abd al-Malik and/or al-Walid I, c. 685–715 CE

where.modern_name: Old City of Jerusalem (proxy pin: UNESCO site coordinates for the whole Old City, not the mosque itself)

importance.justification: One of Islam's holiest sites, central to the Haram al-Sharif and Jerusalem's World Heritage listing.
